Cholera Outbreak Hits Madagascar Gas & Water Utilities Workforce

ANTANANARIVO, Madagascar, June 10—A cholera outbreak among workers in Madagascar’s Gas & Water Utilities industry has disrupted operations at several key facilities, according to officials and industry sources.

The Ministry of Water and Gas confirmed Monday that 74 employees across three regional distribution sites have tested positive for cholera since late May. The affected sites, operated by the utility companies EauxMad and GazMada, are located in the Analamanga and Atsinanana regions. At least 40 of the infected workers remain hospitalized, officials said.

“Protecting our staff is our highest priority. We have implemented emergency health monitoring and sanitation measures across all sites,” said Hery Andrianarivo, spokesperson for EauxMad. “However, with many employees currently absent due to illness or quarantine, our operational capacity is under strain.”

Industry sources said the companies have reduced shift sizes and temporarily halted maintenance activities at two major water treatment plants in Toamasina and Antananarivo. Routine inspection schedules have also been delayed as a result of workforce shortages.

“Our members are working under difficult conditions, and anxiety is high,” said Sahondra Razafindrakoto, president of the Gas & Water Workers’ Union. “We are urging management to provide additional protective equipment and health support.”

The Gas & Water Utilities Regulatory Authority reported that several other sites have increased worker screening and hygiene protocols, but warned that further staff absences are possible in the coming days. “The situation remains fluid,” said authority official Dada Ravelomanana during a press briefing. “We are coordinating closely with public health teams to monitor the outbreak and ensure safe working environments.”

Analysts say the industry’s response will depend on how quickly the outbreak is contained among its workforce. No estimate has been given for when full operations may resume.
